threads.body:
Since the schemas can only describe the JSON form, it'd help to say how producers map them to language types, binary content in particular:

```suggestion
These attributes MUST be recorded as
[AnyValue](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/common/#anyvalue) values
conforming to their JSON schemas.

The JSON schemas describe these attributes when serialized to JSON. Producers
SHOULD use them as a reference for modeling values with language-specific
types. For example, a property with `"format": "binary"` SHOULD be recorded as
a byte array, not a string; it may be encoded during export per the
[AnyValue](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/common/#anyvalue) mapping.
```

The schema still says to base64-encode blob content when serialized, worth dropping in `models.py` and regenerating:

https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/3fe84604a581b3d50dd5b4bd29383b462d2a5018/model/gen-ai/gen-ai-input-messages.json#L37-L42

Optionally, schema tests can accept bytes for `format: binary` too - here's the change with a [test case](https://github.com/lmolkova/semantic-conventions-genai/commit/d4c659a1c2e5eebc317fec0b07c34136964b3327). Happy to send it as a follow-up instead.

replies.body: Can you open an issue for this if my understanding is correct that this is a pre-existing issue? (plain strings are valid AnyValues, though may not conform to a given json schema)

My assumption was that wording was added assuming its a JSON string in many cases. So maybe we can just remove the SHOULD statement there altogether.

I'll have AI figure out why it was added
Resolving, this was intended for instrumentation NOT for consumers. Can file a separate issue on the confusing wording

Looked into git history (open-telemetry/semantic-conventions#2702 and #330) and that `SHOULD` was added because SDKs like OpenAI expose `function.arguments` (and sometimes tool outputs) to instrumentation as a serialized JSON string rather than a parsed dict. Agreed this predates this PR (and #676 covers non-object `gen_ai.tool.call.result`), so I can open a follow-up issue to clean up that note and clarify malformed JSON handling.
